# multi fixture

A small tree with a binary, an empty file, an executable, a path with spaces
and some UTF-8, packed by `tools/repobundle.py` in both formats. The Go bundle
stage must restore it byte for byte and mode for mode.

@@@FILE@@@ 1407 1560a45bd13c5519e1c272766ad17d944645ef49cc1765bfc08d912f7f1ca8c4 644 notes/NOTES.txt
Notes on the multi fixture
==========================

This tree exists to exercise the unpack path in every way a real repository
bundle might: an executable script whose mode must survive, a binary blob
that the text format has to skip and the base64 format has to carry, an
empty file whose header announces zero bytes, a file whose relative path
contains spaces (the bundle header is split into exactly five fields, so the
path may contain any number of them), and a text file with multi-byte UTF-8.

The binary blob is twelve thousand bytes of seeded pseudo-random data. It
does not compress, which keeps the packed bundle honest about size: gzip
gains almost nothing on it, so the frame count in the sender's vectors is
dominated by real payload rather than by repetition.

This file, by contrast, compresses well. Prose is redundant; that is what
lets the sender's gzip stage earn its place in the pipeline. The ratio
reported by `airlift beam` for the whole bundle sits somewhere between the
two extremes, which is what a real repository looks like too: mostly text,
with the occasional image or archive that refuses to shrink.

Nothing here is secret and nothing here matters. If a test fails against
this tree, the test is telling you that the bundle stage changed behaviour,
not that the fixture needs updating. Regenerate the bundles only when the
tree itself changes, and commit both together.
